subject.title: feat(agents): configured agent env reaches spawned subprocesses

question: Should OpenClaw accept broad literal `agents.list[].env` propagation across CLI, exec, ACP/ACPX, and stdio MCP as the canonical agent env API, or prefer the narrower SecretRef/exec-only direction in #96309?
rationale: Both approaches solve real subprocess isolation needs, but they expose different public config contracts and credential-boundary semantics that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Choose the canonical env API before merge
options.body: Pause this PR until maintainers decide whether broad `agents.list[].env` or the narrower #96309 shape should own the public contract.

options.title: Accept broad agent env
options.body: Merge this PR as the canonical sanitized subprocess env surface and treat #96309 as follow-up or refinement work.

options.title: Defer to exec-only SecretRef design
options.body: Close or pause this PR if maintainers want credential injection limited to the narrower exec-only SecretRef model.

recommendation.title: Choose the canonical env API before merge
recommendation.body: Pause this PR until maintainers decide whether broad `agents.list[].env` or the narrower #96309 shape should own the public contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily API and product routing, and prior discussion points to this reviewer for the broad config/env contract direction.
